advice: Experiment: test a two-accumulator schedule using ZA selectors 0 and 1 for two adjacent column tiles of one row tile. For each k, load one A vector and two B vectors, then issue the two FP32 MOPA updates in increasing k order. Store those two tiles before moving to the next row tile. Keep the existing transpose, four FP32 MOPA selector limit, general tail path, and all fixed benchmark rules. This changes the schedule by replacing the 2×2 row-and-column tile with a 1×2 tile; it tests whether fewer live input vectors and a shorter accumulator dependency path improve the loop. It is a proposal only, with no measured evidence of benefit.
risks: The smaller output tile may double row-tile loop work and reduce arithmetic per loaded B value. It may also increase total B traffic. Confirm all four ZA selectors are not needed, handle odd dimensions and incomplete tiles without out-of-bounds loads or stores, check the fixed 0.002 error limit, and compare serially with fresh AC controls. Do not infer a gain from historical noisy scores or assign any joint result to this proposal alone.
